summary: Williamson County, Tennessee fire tower at 962 ft, numbered 7-1 on the state's 1976 list; listed as removed, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed in the Tennessee Landforms tower table; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Numbered 7-1 (district 7, tower 1) on a 1976 state list of towers, per the table's note
Tennessee Landforms table marks the tower removed; no removal year given

evidence.supports: Bingham: Williamson County, 962 ft, state forest number 7-1, marked removed
Table numbers are district-tower state forest numbers from a 1976 list
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers

evidence.supports: The table's sources credit the Division of Forestry with 208 tower sites around 1976
evidence.quote: Division of Forestry (208 tower sites c. 1976, noted in table as distict-tower)

evidence.supports: Table author gave unofficial names to some towers
evidence.quote: I have given unofficial names to towers that were not named on the USGS maps or on the list of towers provided by the state forestry office.

evidence.supports: State tower network formed the physical fire detection network between 1933 and 1975
evidence.quote: Collectively, the fire towers formed the physical manifestation of TDF’s fire detection network between 1933 and 1975.

evidence.supports: By the mid-1970s towers were no longer the mainstay; replaced by quicker and more accurate detection
evidence.quote: In the mid-1970s, TDF fire lookout towers were no longer the mainstay of Tennessee fire control program, having been replaced by quicker and more accurate detection methods.

sources.title: Tennessee Lookout Towers (Tennessee Landforms, Tom Dunigan)
Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers multiple property document
sources.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

notes_for_editor: Identity rests on the Tennessee Landforms table only (waypoint WIT002, 962 ft, Williamson, '7-1 removed'). The table's author says some names are his own, so the name is unverified. No source names an agency for this tower, so the record has none; the state-forest numbering suggests the Division of Forestry but no source states it for this tower. No build date, builder, staffing dates or removal year appear in any source read. Not on the NHLR or FFLOS Tennessee lists (checked 2026-10-21); the Williamson County historic survey excerpt read names Bingham buildings but no tower. The MPS does not mention Bingham by name. Photos: none found.
